About.quote: “Measure what is measurable, and make measurable what is not.”
About.responsibilityText: In many companies, growth depends on a few people, on tools that don't talk to each other and on numbers nobody reads. Our job is to make it observable: understand which levers produce results, decide where to act and turn what works into a system the company can run even without us.

principles.title: Observable
principles.desc: Every action is tied to a number that matters to the business, such as sales, leads or hours saved, not clicks and impressions. You see what works, not just what we did.

principles.title: Governable
principles.desc: At every cycle you receive a written summary: what we saw, what we propose and how confident we are. The decision stays yours.

principles.title: Replicable
principles.desc: What works becomes a process, an automation or software. Documented and owned by you, not tied to a person or a supplier.

results.title: What changed, in practice
beforeAfter: To get a view of the day, the team had to open bookings, chats and spreadsheets, one by one.
One screen shows everything: bookings, passenger lists, messages and guides.
If a message to a customer didn't arrive, the team found out late, often when the customer called.
Messages not delivered on WhatsApp are automatically delivered by SMS, and if that fails a notification appears.
Passenger lists were prepared by hand and sent to guides by email or chat.
Lists become an auto-filled PDF and are shared automatically, in an orderly way, through a link that deletes itself after 24h.
To warn customers about a last-minute change, someone had to message or call them one by one.
An SMS goes out to the customers involved in a few clicks from the dashboard.
Which guide and which driver covered each tour was written in scattered sheets and notes. After the assignment, the most time-consuming part was communicating it.
Guides and drivers are assigned in the calendar, next to the day's bookings, and the driver's screen updates automatically with the information they need.

method.problemsTitle: Our starting analysis and what we changed

problems.label: Audience.
problems.text: Targeting parameters that were too generic, spreading the budget over people with no real intention of getting a tattoo.

problems.label: Campaign setup.
problems.text: Technical settings and budget allocation that needed reworking.

problems.label: Analysis.
problems.text: There was no complete picture of who the customer is and why they choose one studio over another.

analyses.title: Needs and intentions
analyses.desc: We mapped the needs, problems, emotional and rational motivations and search intentions of potential customers.

analyses.title: Obstacles and decision levers
analyses.desc: We identified the barriers and levers that drive a booking, to correct communication and positioning.

analyses.title: Franchise data
analyses.desc: We cross-referenced demographic data with the studios' internal qualitative and quantitative information.

analyses.title: Content and funnel
analyses.desc: The analyses produced the content themes, the funnel structure and tailored offers for each type of customer.

results.title: The numbers before and after
results.text: With the starting point set at 100, here is where leads and acquisition costs ended up.
notes: The −36% is the reduction in cost per lead, while the −20% is the reduction in total budget invested: read together, they show not only a significant saving but, at the same time, a significant increase in results.
70% of classifiable leads concern medium or large projects.

CaseOnlySolutions.googleAdsShareLabel: Of the budget invested in Google Ads
CaseOnlySolutions.contextText: An e-commerce business founded in 2021 to sell technology across Italy, with a catalogue later expanded and distribution extended to Europe and the United States.
CaseOnlySolutions.situationText: When we came in, in 2024: falling revenue, high advertising spend and open technical issues on the website and connected systems.
CaseOnlySolutions.goalText: Relaunch the store ahead of November and December, the months of peak demand, and maximise profit.
CaseOnlySolutions.analysisText: Analysis of the existing strategy and its results; a new setup with lower investment and higher profit from the first month.
CaseOnlySolutions.interventionText: Identifying and fixing issues across the website, applications and connected systems, with a series of technical improvements.
CaseOnlySolutions.optimisationText: Periodic analyses across the related ecosystems reveal points of improvement to act and invest on, steadily boosting performance.
CaseOnlySolutions.shopifyAlt: Shopify dashboard: €687,545.50 in total sales and 2,145 orders from 1 November to 16 December 2024
CaseOnlySolutions.shopifyCaption: Total sales, orders, sessions and conversion rate for the period, compared with the previous six weeks.
CaseOnlySolutions.googleAdsAlt: Google Ads overview from 1 November to 15 December 2024: 66,453 clicks, €3.93 cost per conversion, €0.28 average CPC, €18,300.59 cost
CaseOnlySolutions.googleAdsCaption: The key platform behind the result: about 2/3 of the budget was invested here, with an average return of 81.5 times the spend.
CaseOnlySolutions.roiText: every euro invested in advertising corresponds to €81.50 in revenue.
CaseOnlySolutions.principleText: A return of this kind is only achievable when several ecosystems are managed under one roof, and with precision.
CaseOnlySolutions.ctaTitle: Your advertising budget can return more.
CaseOnlySolutions.ctaText: We analyse your advertising ecosystems and show you where the return can grow.
